context_requirements: Functional estrogen receptor (ESR1 and/or ESR2) expression; ER-positive lineage such as breast (MCF7) or ovarian cells
Intact estrogen response element (ERE) signaling and coactivator availability
For GPER-mediated effects, GPER1 expression and G-protein coupling
Absence of strong antiestrogen/repressive context; ER-negative lines (e.g., HA1E) are expected to be unresponsive
falsifiers: No induction of canonical ER target genes (e.g., PRSS23, GREB1, TFF1, NRIP1) in MCF7 at 6 or 24 h
No difference in transcriptional response between ER-positive (MCF7) and ER-negative (HA1E) lines
Complete absence of any transcriptional change across all nine lines at both timepoints
Response blocked by coincubation with a pure antiestrogen such as fulvestrant/ICI 182,780

evidence.supports: ER-positive T47D cells with an ERE-luciferase reporter respond to ER agonists in a specific, dose-dependent manner, supporting ER-mediated transcriptional activation
In MCF7 cells, 2MEO acts as an ER agonist and most gene expression changes are blocked by the ER antagonist ICI 182,780, confirming ER-dependent transcriptional effects
ER alpha/beta agonists (PPT, DPN) and estrogen modulate inflammatory gene expression and prevent microglial death via ER, supporting ER-dependent anti-inflammatory transcriptional effects
GPER agonist G-1 suppresses proliferation and induces apoptosis in ovarian cancer cells, indicating GPER-mediated antiproliferative effects
G-1 suppresses proliferation and induces apoptosis in a GPER-independent manner, indicating potential off-target antiproliferative effects of some ER/GPER agonists
